name: Caesarea
overview: Caesarea was a significant seaport in Palestine, serving as a strategic and spiritual hub in the early church. It was the home of Philip the evangelist, who preached throughout the region and hosted believers such as Paul (Acts 8:40; 21:8). The city is also notable as the residence of Cornelius, the centurion whose faith opened the gospel to Gentiles (Acts 10:1, 10:24). Additionally, Caesarea was a place where key political figures like Herod and Felix stayed, and where Paul was brought by Roman soldiers to stand trial, highlighting its importance in both the spread of the gospel and the unfolding of God's providence amidst opposition (Acts 12:19; 9:30).
